subject: Recap & next steps — Kyte migration viability for third-party LLM APIs
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Anthony Chang <anthony.chang@kyte.software>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Recap & next steps — Kyte migration viability for third-party LLM APIs

Hi Anthony — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap of what we heard, the risks you called out, and recommended next steps so we have aligned expectations.

Key pain points (from call):
- Vendor lock & cost: ~60% of your prompt spend is with OpenAI + Anthropic; finance flagged growing per-token spend as a top concern.
- Rate limit and availability incidents: two production outages last quarter that impacted user-facing inference.
- Latency variability: some of your short chat queries need <200ms p95 but you see spikes during peak hours.
- Compliance/data residency: EU customer base requires that certain inference and logs remain in eu-west-1.

Current stack (what you shared):
- Generation: OpenAI (GPT-4 variant) for product chat and content gen.
- Safety/moderation: Anthropic for classification/safety checks.
- Embeddings/indexing: OpenAI text-embedding-3-small for semantic search; ingestion pipeline on AWS (eu-west-1).
- Orchestration: in-house API gateway with retry logic and a thin prompt templating layer.

Success criteria you called out:
- Functional parity: outputs should match quality thresholds for our 12 canonical prompts (we'll need your sample set).
- Cost target: reduce per-query inference cost by 40–60% for the bulk of traffic.
- Resilience: avoid single-vendor outages; transparent fallback policy.
- Latency: p95 under 250ms for short chat queries when routed to dedicated capacity.
- Compliance: EU residency for regulated customer data and audit logs.

Preliminary compatibility notes (what to consider for migration):
- Instruction-following models (LLM candidates) will vary on tokenizer, system prompt behavior, and safety outputs — some prompt rewrites and evals are inevitable.
- Embeddings differences will require re-embedding or adapter layers for similarity scores; consider a gradual reindexing plan.
- Safety stack: moving moderation from Anthropic to an open model will require custom fine-tuning / rule-based overlays to match your current thresholds.

Model shortlist we discussed (initial candidates for evaluation):
- LLaMA 3 (70B / 8B variants) — high-quality instruction-following; test for hallucination on your docs.
- Mistral Instruct / Mistral Large — strong instruction tuning on instruction-heavy tasks.
- MosaicML MPT-30B / Instruct variants — cost-effective for mid-size workloads.
- Falcon-180B / RedPajama variants for embeddings + retrieval-heavy workloads (if you need larger context).

Suggested immediate next steps (owner in parenthesis):
1) Share canonical prompt suite + 50 representative production queries + current embedding vectors (Anthony).
2) Grant a read-only sample of your logging/latency traces for the last 30 days (Anthony / infra).
3) Redwood to run a two-week parity eval against shortlist models and return: quality delta, latency profile, and cost estimate (Karthik).
4) Decide on deployment preference: Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) vs Private VPC (if you need on-prem-like residency) — we can scope pricing for both (Aditya).

Attachments: migration checklist and an example latency snapshot (attached).

If this looks right, we propose starting the parity eval the week of Feb 16 and delivering an initial report within 10 business days. Confirm availability for a 30-minute technical kickoff (platform + infra) — suggest Feb 12 or Feb 13.

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Karthik — thanks for the clear write-up, this matches my notes. A few clarifications and additions: 

- Confirmed: OpenAI handles ~62% of token spend (generation + embeddings), Anthropic ~28% (safety + classification).
- Incidents: two rate-limit/outage events in Q4; both lasted ~15–22 minutes but caused retries and some API errors surfaced to users.
- Residency: EU customers require both inference and audit logs to stay in eu-west-1 for a subset of accounts (we can flag those during migration).
- Platform constraints: our infra team prefers AMI/EC2-based deployment; minimal use of proprietary runtimes (we prefer tools we can inspect).
- Internal owners: Priya (Platform), Marco (ML infra), and Sara (Data Compliance) will be part of the technical kickoff.

We can share the 12 canonical prompts and a 50-query sample by EOD Feb 12. For logs, we'll provide sanitized latency traces and a small set of historical requests. Regarding a timeline — Feb 16 start for a parity eval sounds good; we'll aim to be responsive during that two-week window.

Please include a basic ATO/privacy constraints checklist in your kickoff so Sara can validate compliance needs early.

—Anthony
